chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who sees blood in the morning, or after the day has risen, or at noon. He said: She breaks her fast. And if it is after al-ʿaṣr or after noon, then she should continue upon her fast and make up that day.

key_terms.الدَّمَ: the blood indicating the onset of menstruation
key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday or the sun's decline from its zenith
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman about whom the legal ruling is being asked

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman begins menstruation during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a fasting woman who begins menstruation during a day of the month of Ramadan. It distinguishes between the time at which the blood is seen and the practical ruling regarding whether she breaks the fast immediately or completes the day and later makes it up.
